>   carry named a GitLab checkout that is no longer where DevDesk lives.

## Project Overview

DevDesk is a terminal-based TUI (Text User Interface) application built with Go and Bubble Tea framework. It provides DevSecOps functionality including:
- System status monitoring (HTTP/HTTPS, ICMP, DNS, SSL checks)
- GitLab integration (authentication, project explorer, multi-select clone)
- Security scanning (Trivy CVE/secret/license/misconfig + Gitleaks secrets)
- Container management with real-time metrics, on Docker or Podman (`app.container_engine`)
- OCI resource management (image scanning, container launching, network inspection)
- Network diagnostics (DNS, route, ICMP, TCP, TLS, HTTP) + real-time port monitoring + this machine's interfaces + local port forwarding (unprivileged, loopback only)
- Multi-context configuration management via YAML
- Local workspaces management with git metadata
- Claude Code session list (`:agent-usage` / `:au`): sessions found on this machine, by project and date, and per session the agent tree (orchestrator and sub-agents: types, models, tokens, share of the total; sortable by Total; also per agent a state (running / idle / done / unknown, idle after 5 min without a transcript line) shown as a status dot in the first column (the `running` dot blinks, DEVDESK-151) and as text, tool calls and duration; and an indicative cost per agent, `Est. cost` (orange from 75 % and red from 90 % of the session's estimated cost, when at least two agents are priced), from prices you write in the context YAML (`agent_usage.prices`, none shipped), with the session's `Billed` cost and `Unattributed` in the header, DEVDESK-47; a `Breakdown` colour bar per agent and, with `tab` inside a session, a Breakdown tab splitting the whole session's tokens by category, model and agent, as a percentage of tokens, DEVDESK-98). An open session updates live: read again every 2 s while active, only what was appended; paused after 5 min with no write and no unfinished sub-agent, when its transcript is gone, or while the terminal is not focused (header `Updates › paused`, then `paused (terminal not focused)`; `app.when_unfocused: run` keeps it live); `ctrl+r` reads it again in full. The sessions list itself is not live.

## Build and Development Commands

Tasks live in `mise.toml` — there is no Makefile. `mise tasks` lists them all.

```bash
# Development (fastest)
mise run dev          # Run directly with go run
go run .

# Build
mise run build        # Build binary to bin/dk
mise run run          # Build and run

# Testing
mise run test         # Run all tests
mise run cover        # Coverage per package
go test -v ./...      # Run all tests with verbose output
go test ./internal/command  # Run tests for specific package
mise run test-race    # Detect race conditions (critical for Bubble Tea Cmds)

# Code Quality
mise run fmt          # Format code
mise run vet          # Run go vet
mise run lint         # MANDATORY before commits - golangci-lint
mise run tidy         # Tidy dependencies
mise run check        # fmt + vet + lint + test in one go

# Installation
mise run install      # Install to $GOPATH/bin
```

`test-race` needs cgo and therefore a C compiler (`gcc`/`clang`) on `PATH`.

## Git, worktrees, pull requests — absolute rules

- Work happens in a worktree under `.worktrees/<branch>`, created from `origin/main`; the main checkout stays clean, on `main`.
- Never push directly to `main`: the Entire mirror rejects it, and so does the `main-protection` ruleset. Everything goes through a PR, merged once `Lint and build` and `Test` are green.
- Always use `gh -R anthnel/devdesk` (`origin` is `entire://`). There is one remote, `origin`; do not add a second one pointing at GitHub.
- A red `Entire Gates` check caused by Approvals alone does not block a merge (Findings, Checks, Up to date must stay green).
- In a sandbox, only commit; the host pushes, opens the PR and merges. Whoever creates a worktree removes it (never `git worktree prune` from the other side). The sandbox creates its own worktree; the host never creates one for it.
- Before creating a worktree or branch, pushing, opening/merging a PR or removing a worktree, load the `git-worktree-pr` skill.

## Releases

Only merging the release-please PR publishes a release; never merge it without the user's explicit agreement. After every merge on main, the orchestrating session loads the `release-flow` skill and checks the triggers.

### Status Monitoring System

**Factory Pattern for Checkers:**
- `internal/status/checker.go` - Main orchestrator
- `internal/status/http_checker.go` - HTTP/HTTPS checks
- `internal/status/icmp_checker.go` - ICMP ping checks
- `internal/status/dns_checker.go` - DNS resolution checks

Each checker implements `CheckerInterface`. The main `Checker.CheckOne()` uses a factory pattern to instantiate the right checker based on `component.Type`.

**Parallel Execution:**
- `CheckAll()` runs all component checks concurrently using goroutines and sync.WaitGroup
- Results are collected and returned as `[]ComponentStatus`

### Component CRUD Operations

Status view supports adding/editing/deleting monitors:
- `internal/ui/status/components/component_form.go` - Form component
- `internal/ui/status/components/confirm_modal.go` - Confirmation dialog
- Changes persist to `~/.devdesk/config.yaml` via `config.Save()`

State flags in Model: `creating`, `editing`, `confirming`, `selectedIdx`

### Credentials Management

No secret DevDesk holds is written to a file DevDesk owns. `internal/credentials`
implements the `Storage` interface three ways and `Select()` picks exactly one —
writing to several at once is what let the old "secure" option store a token in
the credential manager *and* in plaintext:

| Storage | Backend | Notes |
|---------|---------|-------|
| `KeyringStorage` | Windows Credential Manager / macOS Keychain / Secret Service | via `zalando/go-keyring`, no cgo. The default. |
| `GitCredentialStorage` | git's configured credential helper | Only when the helper is not `store`, which writes plaintext. Context-aware. |
| `MemoryStorage` | this process | Last resort, and deliberately worse: the auth view says nothing was saved. |

`Select(context, preference)` returns a `Selection{Storage, Backend, Detail}`.
The order is keyring → git credential → memory; `app.secret_backend` in the
context config pins the head of it (`auto`, `keyring`, `git-credential`). A
pinned backend that is unreachable falls through to memory rather than silently
to the other one.

The router resolves one `Selection` per context and keeps it in
`shared.State.Secrets`. It must be reused for the lifetime of the context — a
second `Select()` call yields a fresh `MemoryStorage` that cannot see what the
first one holds.

`MigrateLegacySecrets` runs at startup and on every context switch: a
`gitlab.token` or `registry.password` left in a context file by an older build
is moved into the store and deleted from the YAML, with the result reported in
the auth view.

## Testing

Test files follow Go conventions (`*_test.go`):
- `internal/command/parser_test.go` - Command parser tests
- `internal/app/app_test.go` - App router tests

Use table-driven tests where appropriate.

**`go test` does not detect races or explore fuzz targets.** `mise run test` runs
only the fuzz seeds, so `internal/agentusage` concurrency tests
(`TestConcurrent*`) need `mise run test-race`. To explore `FuzzIncrementalMatchesFull`
run `go test -fuzz=FuzzIncrementalMatchesFull -fuzztime=60s ./internal/agentusage`.

**HOME is shared across a test process.** `TestMain` in `internal/app` sets
`HOME` once for the whole process, so under `go test -count=N` a test finds
the files its own previous run wrote (context config, forge index cache), and
it fails from `-count=2` while `-count=1` passes (DEVDESK-36). A test that
writes under HOME isolates it with `t.Setenv("HOME", t.TempDir())` and
`USERPROFILE` too; in `internal/app`, call `isolateHome(t)` from
`harness_test.go` (already done by `routerAt`). `internal/ui/setup` is fixed
(DEVDESK-38): its `isolateHome(t)` helper in `model_test.go` is called by the
tests that write under HOME. Other packages whose TestMain does
`os.Setenv("HOME", …)` may have the same default. To find them:
`grep -rn 'os.Setenv("HOME"' --include=*_test.go`, then `go test -count=2` on each package.

**Never get a "free" port by `net.Listen("tcp", "127.0.0.1:0")`, reading the
port, then `Close()`, and letting the code under test bind it later.** Between
the close and the bind, any `bind(0)` can be handed that very port: an
`httptest.NewServer` in the same test, another test, another process on the
runner. The symptom is an intermittent `address already in use`, mostly in CI
(Linux gave the just-closed port back to about 1 `bind(0)` in 7,000; DEVDESK-35,
D85 in `docs/backlog.md`).

- If the code under test takes a port, call `loopback.ReservePort(t)`
  (`internal/testutil/loopback`). On Linux it holds a socket bound with
  `SO_REUSEADDR`, never listening, until `t.Cleanup`: `bind(0)` and `connect()`
  cannot take the port, but `net.Listen` can.
- Otherwise let the server bind `:0` and read the real port, or keep the
  listener open and hand it to the code under test.
- Off Linux, `ReservePort` keeps the old behavior and the window stays open
  (on Windows Go does not set `SO_REUSEADDR`). That is known, not a local bug.
- `internal/testutil/loopback` is imported from `_test.go` files only; nothing
  enforces it yet.

**Test input and colour (DEVDESK-199).** Build keys only through
`internal/ui/testutil` (`Key`, `Keys`, `Type`, `Paste`, `Text`, `IsText`), never a
literal `tea.KeyPressMsg` or `tea.Key*`. `Key` returns a
`tea.KeyPressMsg` (`Keys` and `Type` return a message list), `Paste` a `tea.PasteMsg`; `Key` is strict: an unknown name
panics. The space key is built as a key (`Key("space")`), never matched through
`String()` (v1 `" "`, v2 `"space"`). Lip Gloss v2 has no global colour profile (`Style.Render` always emits full
colour), so a test needs no setup to check styling; it reads the SGR or strips it
with `ansi.Strip`. `internal/ui/testutil/source_guard_test.go` fails the suite on a
hand-built key, a `colorprofile` import outside `internal/app/profile_test.go` and
`internal/app/redraw_measure_test.go` or `SetColorProfile` in any `_test.go`. Paste tests
(`internal/app/paste_test.go`, `wrapped_input_test.go`, `component_form_test.go`):
a paste reaches the focused field, newlines become spaces in single-line fields,
and no key action fires (Rule 111).

**Space and key API (DEVDESK-200).** Production code matches the space key as
`keymap.Space`, never `" "`/`"space"`, and reads keys through `String()` only
(no `.Runes`, `.Alt`, `.Paste`, `tea.KeyType` or `tea.Key<Name>`). Update
handlers switch on `tea.KeyPressMsg`, never the `tea.KeyMsg` interface (it also
matches releases). A paste is a `tea.PasteMsg`, not a key (Rule 111). Guards in
`internal/ui/keymap` (`space_scan_test.go`, `legacy_key_scan_test.go`,
`viewport_keymap_scan_test.go`) fail the suite otherwise; limits are listed in
`docs/architecture/app-shell.md`.

## Critical Bubble Tea Rules

**NEVER modify model state inside a Cmd** (Rule 110) - Race condition:
- `Update()` is the ONLY place to modify model state
- `View()` is read-only
- `Cmd` functions do I/O and return messages

**NEVER use `style.Render()` inside `table.Row{}`** (Rule 122) - ANSI sequences corrupt all subsequent rows:
- Use plain text: `theme.IconError + " error"` not `theme.StatusErrorStyle.Render(...)`
- Apply row styling via `table.SetStyles(theme.TableStylesForState("error"))`

**Views render through `Render()`** (Bubble Tea v2): a top-level view implements
`Render() string` and `View() tea.View { return tea.NewView(m.Render()) }`; only the
router (`App.View()`) sets terminal state such as `AltScreen` and `BackgroundColor`. Components keep
`View() string`. Colours are `color.Color`; hex literals stay in `theme/colors.go`.

**Update() case extraction**: If a case block exceeds 5 lines, extract to `handle[MessageType]()` method returning `(tea.Model, tea.Cmd)`

| [`tui-tables.md`](tui-tables.md) | 106, 116, 122, 125, 136, 139 | Tables, column widths, plain-text cells + color via `Style`, filter bar, body never replaced (spinner or message) |

## Critical rules (summary)

**Rule 110** — NEVER modify the model inside a `Cmd` → race condition. Only `Update()` modifies the model.

**Rule 122** — `Cell` returns plain text (it gets measured), color goes through `Style`. A `style.Render(...)` inside `Cell` gets truncated in the middle of its escape sequence and bleeds onto every following row.

**Rule 128** — A footer message goes through `components.FooterMessage`: three levels (neutral info, orange warning, red error), always centered, a single implementation. A table's loading state is shown in the footer, never in the body: with `Spinner` + `SetSpinnerFrame` for a view's own loading, with the shared activity dot (`Status.Activity`, `●`/`○`, `SetBlinkPhase`) for work the router tracks. A new `Activity` value not driven by the jobs registry must implement `WantsBlink()`, or the dot stays fixed.

**Rule 139** — A `datatable`'s body is always `m.table.View()`, never a spinner or a message: an empty table (loading, nothing to list, a filter with no results) stays a table — a header, no rows. The count goes in `GetHeaderInfo`, the status in the footer.

**Rule 129** — All UI text and all logs in **English US**.

**Rule 140** — An invalid form field is underlined through `theme.StyleInvalidField` (the only entry point to the underline API), and the error is also in the footer at level Error, derived on every render. The underline is never the only carrier.

**Rule 133** — `bubbles/textarea` is forbidden. Use `components.WrappedInput` for any multi-line text field.

## Work starts in a new worktree

**Any task that will produce a commit begins with its own worktree**, cut from
the current `main`, **under `.worktrees/` inside the repository**:

```bash
git fetch origin main
git worktree add -b <branch> .worktrees/<branch> origin/main
cd .worktrees/<branch>
```

Answering a question, reading code, running the app — none of that needs one.
Editing does.

**Under the repository, not beside it.** This reverses what this file said until
now, and the reason it gave was wrong. It claimed a worktree at `.worktrees/x`
would be compiled by `go build ./...` and `go test ./...`. It would not: the go
tool skips every directory whose name begins with `.` or `_`, so `.worktrees/`
is invisible to `./...`. Verified rather than assumed — a package of deliberately
invalid Go placed under `.worktrees/` builds clean and `go list ./...` does not
name it. The old argument holds for `worktrees/` without the dot, which is
presumably where it came from.

What decides it is the **sandbox mount**, and it cost a full debugging session to
find. A direct-mode sandbox mounts *this directory only*. A sibling worktree at
`../devdesk-<branch>` is therefore outside the mount, so its **files** are written
into the container's private layer and never reach the host — while `.git` is
inside the mount and stays shared. Refs agree, files diverge, and nothing warns:
the branch tip moves, the host's copy of those files does not, and `git status`
on the host reports the *stale* content as uncommitted modifications. An agent
and the person testing its work end up compiling different code while both
believe they are on the same branch. Under `.worktrees/`, host and sandbox see
one filesystem.

Two effects worth knowing, neither blocking:

- `.worktrees/` is in `.gitignore`; a worktree there is not a change to the tree.
- Claude Code discovers the nested `.claude/` of each worktree, so its skills and
  rules appear a second time, prefixed by the worktree path. Harmless, and the
  price of the directory being inside the repo.

**What isolates, and what does not.** git refuses to check out one branch in two
worktrees, so two agents cannot land on the same branch by accident — that is the
whole protection, and it is worth knowing what it does *not* cover:

| Shared by every worktree | Consequence |
|---|---|
| `~/.devdesk/` — contexts, `config.yaml`, scan caches | two agents editing settings or scanning at once overwrite each other's; nothing warns |
| the host keyring, Docker, the ports the app binds | one at a time, whoever gets there first |
| `.git/hooks` | verified: `git rev-parse --git-path hooks` resolves to the **main** checkout's, so the Entire checkpoint and pre-push hooks fire normally from a worktree |
| `origin` | inherited — `git push -u origin <branch>` goes through the mirror as usual |

`mise` tasks and `go build` work unchanged; both read the tree they are run in.

**`entire graph` indexes per directory.** A fresh worktree has no index, so the
first `entire graph search` there pays a full build (~5 s on this repo, measured)
and the symbol ids it returns are namespaced by the directory name
(`local/<branch>:Go:…`). Nothing breaks; do not be surprised by the first search
being slow or by ids that do not match another worktree's.

**Clean up when the PR is merged**, from the main checkout:

```bash
git worktree remove .worktrees/<branch>
git worktree list          # what is still out there
git worktree prune         # after a directory was deleted by hand
```

`git worktree remove` refuses a tree with uncommitted changes, which is the
point — look before forcing.

**The main checkout stays on `main` and stays clean.** It is what `git fetch
origin main && git merge --ff-only origin/main` needs after each merge, and what
every new worktree is cut from.

## Git workflow — pull requests only

**Never push directly to `main`.** The Entire mirror rejects it:

```
! [remote rejected] main -> main (protected branch)
```

This is enforced by the mirror, not by GitHub, and **Entire does not document it**
— neither the CLI help nor `docs.entire.io` mentions a protected default branch.
The only branch restriction Entire states is that `entire/unmirrored/*` is never
forwarded. Treat the rejection as observed behaviour, not as a specified one.

**The repository is public since 2026-09-06**, which is what makes GitHub-side
enforcement possible at all: a private repo on a free personal plan answers
`403 Upgrade to GitHub Pro or make this repository public` on both
`/repos/anthnel/devdesk/branches/main/protection` and
`/repos/anthnel/devdesk/rulesets` — that was the prior state, and it is not a
description to trust going forward if the repo ever goes private again. Do not
cite `gh api repos/anthnel/devdesk/branches/main` reporting `"protected":
false` as proof of anything either way: that field only ever reflects legacy
branch protection, so it reads `false` under a ruleset too, and it read `false`
on the free-private plan whatever the configuration. Query
`/repos/anthnel/devdesk/rulesets` itself (or `gh ruleset check main`) for the
real answer.

A ruleset named `main-protection` (id `22399372`) now targets `refs/heads/main`
only — deliberately not `entire/checkpoints/v1`, which receives automatic
pushes from the Entire hook and would break if rule-gated. It requires a pull
request (0 approving reviews — solo maintainer, the PR is a record not a review
gate) with the `Lint and build` and `Test` checks from `ci.yml` passing,
blocks force-pushes and branch deletion, and grants no bypass. This closes the
gap the mirror alone left open: the Entire mirror's rejection of a direct push
to `main` was, until now, the *only* protection — a second remote pointing
straight at GitHub would have sailed through (see the warning against adding
one, below). Now GitHub itself refuses that push too.

**The `Entire Gates` check is expected to stay red on this repository.** It is
a PR check from the `entire` app, and its **Approvals** gate fails until another
reviewer approves the trail. That approval cannot arrive: the repository has one
developer, so the gate cannot be green, and no second account or dummy reviewer
should be added to satisfy it. The check is not required by `main-protection`
(GitHub reports the PR as `UNSTABLE` but `MERGEABLE`), so a red `Entire Gates`
alone does not block a merge. Merge once `Lint and build` and `Test` pass. The
Findings, Checks and Up to date gates must stay green: if any of them fails, it
is a real signal, so stop and raise it with the user. Agents (orchestrator,
devops) must not stop to ask for agreement over the Approvals failure alone.
To read the reason:
`gh api repos/anthnel/devdesk/commits/<sha>/check-runs --jq '.check_runs[] | select(.name=="Entire Gates") | .output.summary'`.

Every other branch, including `entire/checkpoints/v1`, pushes through the mirror
and is forwarded to GitHub.

**Pull requests are GitHub's, not Entire's.** Entire has no merge-request
concept — it layers checkpoints and sessions over git and forwards pushes. So
the PR steps below are `gh`, and the branch they review is one `origin` carried
to GitHub. `entire review` (labs) runs a multi-agent review against the current
branch and is a pre-merge step, not a substitute for the PR.

```bash
git worktree add -b <branch> .worktrees/<branch> origin/main   # work happens here
git push -u origin <branch>                     # via the mirror — forwarded to GitHub
gh pr create -R anthnel/devdesk --base main --head <branch>
gh pr merge -R anthnel/devdesk <n> --squash --delete-branch
# then, from the main checkout:
git fetch origin main && git merge --ff-only origin/main   # may need a retry, see below
git worktree remove .worktrees/<branch>
```

**`-R anthnel/devdesk` is not optional.** `gh` infers the repository from a
remote pointing at a GitHub host, and `origin` is an `entire://` URL, so it
finds none and fails with *"none of the git remotes configured for this
repository point to a known GitHub host"*. The flag names the repo directly.
Do not solve this by adding a GitHub remote — see below.

**After a merge, `origin` can read stale for a minute or two.** The mirror lags
GitHub, so `git fetch origin` right after `gh pr merge` may return the *previous*
`main` — with no error, which is the part that misleads. `gh pr view <n> --json state`
says `MERGED` while `git rev-parse origin/main` still points at the commit before
it. Re-run the fetch a moment later; `gh` is what to trust in the meantime,
because it talks to GitHub directly and needs no remote.

**Do not add a second remote pointing at GitHub to work around that.** The
`main-protection` ruleset (above) would now refuse a direct `git push github
main` too, so it is no longer the *only* defeat of the only protection — but a
direct push still bypasses the mirror, and with it the Entire hook that
records checkpoints and sessions, which is not visible until much later.
`origin` is the only remote, deliberately.

**Merging several branches cut from the same commit conflicts in
`docs/backlog.md`.** Every fix inserts its entry at the top of §1.1, so the
second and third merges land on the same anchor. The resolution is always to
keep both sides — they are independent entries, not competing edits.


**A follow-up commit on the same branch, after the first one already got
squash-merged, will conflict on a plain `git merge`** — squashing rewrites
history, so `git merge origin/main` computes the wrong common ancestor
(the branch's *own* pre-squash parent) and re-diffs files that already
landed, even when nothing actually conflicts in substance. Don't hand-edit
through that; cherry-pick the new commit straight onto current `origin/main`
instead — its real parent already matches what's on `main`, so it applies
clean:

```bash
git worktree add -b <tmp-branch> .worktrees/<tmp-branch> <new-sha>
cd .worktrees/<tmp-branch>
git reset --hard origin/main
git cherry-pick <new-sha>              # clean apply — verify before trusting this
go build ./... && go test ./<touched-packages>/...
git push origin HEAD:refs/heads/<new-branch-name>
# gh pr create / gh pr merge as above, then from the main checkout:
git worktree remove .worktrees/<tmp-branch>
```

### Remotes

| Remote | URL | Use |
|--------|-----|-----|
| `origin` | `entire://aws-eu-central-1.entire.io/gh/anthnel/devdesk` | Entire mirror — everything: clone, fetch, push |

**There is one remote, and there should stay one.** The repository is hosted on
GitHub and mirrored to EntireDB in `aws-eu-central-1` (a second placement exists
in `aws-us-east-2`), but every git operation goes through the mirror: it is the
regional path, it is what keeps agent reads fast, and it is where the checkpoint
hook runs. Anything needing GitHub's own answer — PR state, review threads —
goes through `gh`, which authenticates directly and does not need a remote.

Semantic search (`entire search`, and the `entire:*` skills that depend on it) is
**not available in the EU region** — the server answers `semantic search is not
yet available in the region(s) hosting this search`. Nothing in the repo config
fixes this.

The sandbox/host relay (landing a sandbox-made commit, developing in the sandbox and testing from the host) is in [sandbox.md](sandbox.md); read it only when a sandbox is involved.

After the merge, load the `release-flow` skill.

Tu gères la chaîne de livraison : du commit à la production.

## Intégration et release

Charge la skill `dev-team:git-workflow` avant toute branche, commit, PR/MR, tag ou
release : nommage, Conventional Commits, gabarit de PR, commandes `gh` / `glab`, semver,
Keep a Changelog. Les conventions du projet priment.

## CI/CD et infra

- Pipelines reproductibles : actions et images épinglées, cache, permissions minimales.
- Secrets uniquement via le gestionnaire de secrets de la plateforme.
- Docker : images minimales, utilisateur non root, multi-stage.

## Plane

Si ces outils sont listés sans schéma, charge-les d'abord avec `ToolSearch`
(`select:mcp__plane-devops__workitem,mcp__plane-devops__workitem_comment`) avant de conclure
qu'ils sont absents.

Si le brief donne un work item Plane et que les outils `mcp__plane-devops__*` sont
disponibles (identifiants d'états dans la section `## Plane` de `CLAUDE.md`) :
- mets l'identifiant (ex. `DEVDESK-12`) dans le nom de branche et le titre de la PR ;
- ajoute la PR ou MR en lien sur la story (`workitem_link create`, titre `PR #<n>` ou
  `MR !<n>`) ;
- après le merge, passe la story en Done et commente la version ou le tag livré.

Rien d'autre : ni création, ni suppression, ni archivage.

## Garde-fous

Demande confirmation avant toute action difficile à annuler ou visible de l'extérieur :
push, merge, tag, release, déploiement, modification d'infra, `--force`. Rapporte
l'état réel (statut CI, URL de PR), jamais supposé.

## Ne rien supposer

Si une information qui change le résultat manque ou est ambiguë (cible de déploiement, remote ou dépôt, numéro de version, environnement, secret à utiliser), ne la devine
pas : arrête-toi et rends tes questions en tête de ta sortie, sous **Questions

les posera à l'utilisateur. Pour un détail sans conséquence, choisis l'option la plus
prudente et signale-la dans ta sortie (`Hypothèse : …`).

content.text:
Base directory for this skill: C:\Users\anthoni\projects\entire\anthnel\devdesk\.claude\skills\git-worktree-pr

## Work starts in a new worktree

**Any task that will produce a commit begins with its own worktree**, cut from
the current `main`, **under `.worktrees/` inside the repository**:

```bash
git fetch origin main
git worktree add -b <branch> .worktrees/<branch> origin/main
cd .worktrees/<branch>
```

Answering a question, reading code, running the app — none of that needs one.
Editing does.

**Under the repository, not beside it.** This reverses what this file said until
now, and the reason it gave was wrong. It claimed a worktree at `.worktrees/x`
would be compiled by `go build ./...` and `go test ./...`. It would not: the go
tool skips every directory whose name begins with `.` or `_`, so `.worktrees/`
is invisible to `./...`. Verified rather than assumed — a package of deliberately
invalid Go placed under `.worktrees/` builds clean and `go list ./...` does not
name it. The old argument holds for `worktrees/` without the dot, which is
presumably where it came from.

What decides it is the **sandbox mount**, and it cost a full debugging session to
find. A direct-mode sandbox mounts *this directory only*. A sibling worktree at
`../devdesk-<branch>` is therefore outside the mount, so its **files** are written
into the container's private layer and never reach the host — while `.git` is
inside the mount and stays shared. Refs agree, files diverge, and nothing warns:
the branch tip moves, the host's copy of those files does not, and `git status`
on the host reports the *stale* content as uncommitted modifications. An agent
and the person testing its work end up compiling different code while both
believe they are on the same branch. Under `.worktrees/`, host and sandbox see
one filesystem.

Two effects worth knowing, neither blocking:

- `.worktrees/` is in `.gitignore`; a worktree there is not a change to the tree.
- Claude Code discovers the nested `.claude/` of each worktree, so its skills and
  rules appear a second time, prefixed by the worktree path. Harmless, and the
  price of the directory being inside the repo.

**What isolates, and what does not.** git refuses to check out one branch in two
worktrees, so two agents cannot land on the same branch by accident — that is the
whole protection, and it is worth knowing what it does *not* cover:

| Shared by every worktree | Consequence |
|---|---|
| `~/.devdesk/` — contexts, `config.yaml`, scan caches | two agents editing settings or scanning at once overwrite each other's; nothing warns |
| the host keyring, Docker, the ports the app binds | one at a time, whoever gets there first |
| `.git/hooks` | verified: `git rev-parse --git-path hooks` resolves to the **main** checkout's, so the Entire checkpoint and pre-push hooks fire normally from a worktree |
| `origin` | inherited — `git push -u origin <branch>` goes through the mirror as usual |

`mise` tasks and `go build` work unchanged; both read the tree they are run in.

**`entire graph` indexes per directory.** A fresh worktree has no index, so the
first `entire graph search` there pays a full build (~5 s on this repo, measured)
and the symbol ids it returns are namespaced by the directory name
(`local/<branch>:Go:…`). Nothing breaks; do not be surprised by the first search
being slow or by ids that do not match another worktree's.

**Clean up when the PR is merged**, from the main checkout:

```bash
git worktree remove .worktrees/<branch>
git worktree list          # what is still out there
git worktree prune         # after a directory was deleted by hand
```

`git worktree remove` refuses a tree with uncommitted changes, which is the
point — look before forcing.

**The main checkout stays on `main` and stays clean.** It is what `git fetch
origin main && git merge --ff-only origin/main` needs after each merge, and what
every new worktree is cut from.

## Git workflow — pull requests only

**Never push directly to `main`.** The Entire mirror rejects it:

```
! [remote rejected] main -> main (protected branch)
```

This is enforced by the mirror, not by GitHub, and **Entire does not document it**
— neither the CLI help nor `docs.entire.io` mentions a protected default branch.
The only branch restriction Entire states is that `entire/unmirrored/*` is never
forwarded. Treat the rejection as observed behaviour, not as a specified one.

**The repository is public since 2026-09-06**, which is what makes GitHub-side
enforcement possible at all: a private repo on a free personal plan answers
`403 Upgrade to GitHub Pro or make this repository public` on both
`/repos/anthnel/devdesk/branches/main/protection` and
`/repos/anthnel/devdesk/rulesets` — that was the prior state, and it is not a
description to trust going forward if the repo ever goes private again. Do not
cite `gh api repos/anthnel/devdesk/branches/main` reporting `"protected":
false` as proof of anything either way: that field only ever reflects legacy
branch protection, so it reads `false` under a ruleset too, and it read `false`
on the free-private plan whatever the configuration. Query
`/repos/anthnel/devdesk/rulesets` itself (or `gh ruleset check main`) for the
real answer.

A ruleset named `main-protection` (id `22399372`) now targets `refs/heads/main`
only — deliberately not `entire/checkpoints/v1`, which receives automatic
pushes from the Entire hook and would break if rule-gated. It requires a pull
request (0 approving reviews — solo maintainer, the PR is a record not a review
gate) with the `Lint and build` and `Test` checks from `ci.yml` passing,
blocks force-pushes and branch deletion, and grants no bypass. This closes the
gap the mirror alone left open: the Entire mirror's rejection of a direct push
to `main` was, until now, the *only* protection — a second remote pointing
straight at GitHub would have sailed through (see the warning against adding
one, below). Now GitHub itself refuses that push too.

**The `Entire Gates` check is expected to stay red on this repository.** It is
a PR check from the `entire` app, and its **Approvals** gate fails until another
reviewer approves the trail. That approval cannot arrive: the repository has one
developer, so the gate cannot be green, and no second account or dummy reviewer
should be added to satisfy it. The check is not required by `main-protection`
(GitHub reports the PR as `UNSTABLE` but `MERGEABLE`), so a red `Entire Gates`
alone does not block a merge. Merge once `Lint and build` and `Test` pass. The
Findings, Checks and Up to date gates must stay green: if any of them fails, it
is a real signal, so stop and raise it with the user. Agents (orchestrator,
devops) must not stop to ask for agreement over the Approvals failure alone.
To read the reason:
`gh api repos/anthnel/devdesk/commits/<sha>/check-runs --jq '.check_runs[] | select(.name=="Entire Gates") | .output.summary'`.

Every other branch, including `entire/checkpoints/v1`, pushes through the mirror
and is forwarded to GitHub.

**Pull requests are GitHub's, not Entire's.** Entire has no merge-request
concept — it layers checkpoints and sessions over git and forwards pushes. So
the PR steps below are `gh`, and the branch they review is one `origin` carried
to GitHub. `entire review` (labs) runs a multi-agent review against the current
branch and is a pre-merge step, not a substitute for the PR.

```bash
git worktree add -b <branch> .worktrees/<branch> origin/main   # work happens here
git push -u origin <branch>                     # via the mirror — forwarded to GitHub
gh pr create -R anthnel/devdesk --base main --head <branch>
gh pr merge -R anthnel/devdesk <n> --squash --delete-branch
# then, from the main checkout:
git fetch origin main && git merge --ff-only origin/main   # may need a retry, see below
git worktree remove .worktrees/<branch>
```

**`-R anthnel/devdesk` is not optional.** `gh` infers the repository from a
remote pointing at a GitHub host, and `origin` is an `entire://` URL, so it
finds none and fails with *"none of the git remotes configured for this
repository point to a known GitHub host"*. The flag names the repo directly.
Do not solve this by adding a GitHub remote — see below.

**After a merge, `origin` can read stale for a minute or two.** The mirror lags
GitHub, so `git fetch origin` right after `gh pr merge` may return the *previous*
`main` — with no error, which is the part that misleads. `gh pr view <n> --json state`
says `MERGED` while `git rev-parse origin/main` still points at the commit before
it. Re-run the fetch a moment later; `gh` is what to trust in the meantime,
because it talks to GitHub directly and needs no remote.

**Do not add a second remote pointing at GitHub to work around that.** The
`main-protection` ruleset (above) would now refuse a direct `git push github
main` too, so it is no longer the *only* defeat of the only protection — but a
direct push still bypasses the mirror, and with it the Entire hook that
records checkpoints and sessions, which is not visible until much later.
`origin` is the only remote, deliberately.

**Merging several branches cut from the same commit conflicts in
`docs/backlog.md`.** Every fix inserts its entry at the top of §1.1, so the
second and third merges land on the same anchor. The resolution is always to
keep both sides — they are independent entries, not competing edits.


**A follow-up commit on the same branch, after the first one already got
squash-merged, will conflict on a plain `git merge`** — squashing rewrites
history, so `git merge origin/main` computes the wrong common ancestor
(the branch's *own* pre-squash parent) and re-diffs files that already
landed, even when nothing actually conflicts in substance. Don't hand-edit
through that; cherry-pick the new commit straight onto current `origin/main`
instead — its real parent already matches what's on `main`, so it applies
clean:

```bash
git worktree add -b <tmp-branch> .worktrees/<tmp-branch> <new-sha>
cd .worktrees/<tmp-branch>
git reset --hard origin/main
git cherry-pick <new-sha>              # clean apply — verify before trusting this
go build ./... && go test ./<touched-packages>/...
git push origin HEAD:refs/heads/<new-branch-name>
# gh pr create / gh pr merge as above, then from the main checkout:
git worktree remove .worktrees/<tmp-branch>
```

### Remotes

| Remote | URL | Use |
|--------|-----|-----|
| `origin` | `entire://aws-eu-central-1.entire.io/gh/anthnel/devdesk` | Entire mirror — everything: clone, fetch, push |

**There is one remote, and there should stay one.** The repository is hosted on
GitHub and mirrored to EntireDB in `aws-eu-central-1` (a second placement exists
in `aws-us-east-2`), but every git operation goes through the mirror: it is the
regional path, it is what keeps agent reads fast, and it is where the checkpoint
hook runs. Anything needing GitHub's own answer — PR state, review threads —
goes through `gh`, which authenticates directly and does not need a remote.

Semantic search (`entire search`, and the `entire:*` skills that depend on it) is
**not available in the EU region** — the server answers `semantic search is not
yet available in the region(s) hosting this search`. Nothing in the repo config
fixes this.

The sandbox/host relay (landing a sandbox-made commit, developing in the sandbox and testing from the host) is in [sandbox.md](sandbox.md); read it only when a sandbox is involved.

After the merge, load the `release-flow` skill.

# Spike Linux natif (S-01, DEVDESK-325 / DEVDESK-385) : rapport de mesure

Prototype jetable, branche `spike/nettrace` (jamais fusionnée), commit `11cead91`, code dans `spike/nettrace/main.go` (stdlib seule, `syscall`, aucune dépendance `x/sys`, IPv4 seul). Un socket UDP par TTL (1 à 30), tous les sondes partent en parallèle, `IP_TTL` + `IP_RECVERR` posés dans `net.Dialer.Control`, lecture de la file d'erreurs par `RawConn.Read` (netpoller) avec `recvmsg(MSG_ERRQUEUE|MSG_DONTWAIT)`, annulation par `context`.

## Environnement (lu sur la machine par le binaire)

| Élément | Valeur |
|---|---|
| Machine | `datomir`, utilisateur `anthoni` (non-root, aucun `sudo`, aucun `setcap`) |
| OS | Debian GNU/Linux 13 (trixie), linux/amd64 |
| Noyau | 6.12.94+deb13-amd64 |
| Go (compilation) | go1.27.4 (`CGO_ENABLED=0`, binaire ELF statique, vérifié par `file`) |
| uid / CapEff | 1000 / `0000000000000000` |
| Cible publique | `1.1.1.1` (paramètre `-target`) ; cible muette `192.0.2.1` (paramètre `-unreachable`) |
| Durée de sonde | 3 s (`-probe-timeout`), délai global 30 s, TTL max 30 |
| Exécutions | 5 exécutions complètes, plus 1 exécution à `PATH` vide |

## Commande exacte de reproduction

```sh
git checkout spike/nettrace   # commit 11cead91
SHA=$(git rev-parse --short HEAD)
GOOS=linux GOARCH=amd64 CGO_ENABLED=0 go build -ldflags "-X main.commit=$SHA" -o nettrace ./spike/nettrace
scp nettrace anthoni@datomir:<dossier temporaire>/
ssh anthoni@datomir 'cd <dossier temporaire> && ./nettrace'                 # x5
ssh anthoni@datomir 'cd <dossier temporaire> && env -i PATH= ./nettrace'    # L1 (c)
# le binaire trace 1.1.1.1 ; options : -target -unreachable -max-ttl -probe-timeout -deadline -cycles -extra-targets
```

Le binaire a ensuite été supprimé de `datomir` (dossier temporaire retiré). Rien d'autre n'y a été installé ni modifié. Le rapport contient les adresses des routeurs ; les adresses ci-dessous sont celles de la mesure, à relire avant de coller ailleurs.

## Mesures brutes

### Chemin vers 1.1.1.1 (exécution 1, 11 sauts)

TTL 1 `192.168.1.1` 3.34 ms ; 2 `192.168.0.1` 3.03 ms ; 3 `10.133.114.1` 14.93 ms ; 4 `10.239.252.179` 15.69 ms ; 5 `212.224.245.178` 16.68 ms ; 6 `212.224.245.177` 16.84 ms ; 7 muet ; 8 `212.224.130.204` 19.30 ms ; 9 `162.158.232.6` 23.72 ms ; 10 `162.158.232.19` 28.37 ms ; 11 `1.1.1.1` 19.10 ms (cible atteinte, Port Unreachable).

### Tableau par exécution

| Exécution | Résultat du trace principal | Sauts avec adresse | TTL muets | Cible atteinte au TTL | Durée |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | cible atteinte | 10 | 7 | 11 | 3.001 s |
| 2 | cible atteinte | 7 | 7 à 22 | 23 | 3.001 s |
| 3 | cible non atteinte, TTL maximum | 6 | 7 à 30 | - | 3.003 s |
| 4 | cible atteinte | 7 | 7 à 15 | 16 | 3.003 s |
| 5 | cible non atteinte, TTL maximum | 6 | 7 à 30 | - | 3.004 s |
| `PATH` vide | cible atteinte | 9 | 1, 7, 11 à 19 | 20 | 3.001 s |

Constat non prévu : le nombre de sauts qui répondent varie d'une exécution à l'autre (6 à 10), et le TTL de la cible atteinte varie (11, 23, 16, 20, ou jamais). Hypothèse (non vérifiée) : limitation du débit des ICMP par des routeurs ou par la cible face à 30 sondes simultanées. Conséquence : le « TTL le plus bas qui atteint la cible » n'est pas le nombre réel de sauts du chemin (11 dans l'exécution 1).

### L1 : sans privilège, sans binaire externe, sans conteneur

| Mesure | Résultat |
|---|---|
| uid, CapEff (6 exécutions) | 1000, `0000000000000000` |
| `setsockopt` `IP_TTL` / `IP_RECVERR` | aucune erreur (`EPERM` jamais vu), 6 exécutions |
| imports directs (`GOOS=linux go list -f '{{.Imports}}' ./spike/nettrace`) | `context encoding/binary errors flag fmt net net/netip os runtime sort strings sync syscall time` : pas d'`os/exec` |
| `PATH` vide (`env -i PATH=`) | même résultat que `PATH` normal, tous verdicts OK |
| conteneur | aucun démarré, aucun moteur utilisé |

### L2 : au moins 3 sauts avec adresse, TTL croissants

Sauts avec adresse : 10, 7, 6, 7, 6 (exécutions 1 à 5). Ordre croissant de TTL : vrai dans les 5. Minimum 6 >= 3.

### L3 : netpoller

Lecture par `RawConn.Read`, aucun `time.Sleep` ni boucle d'attente dans le code de lecture. Attente maximale d'une sonde qui a reçu une réponse, pour un délai de lecture de 3 s : 28.4, 30.9, 75.4, 107.2, 131.3 ms (exécutions 1 à 5). Note : la « latence » et l'attente sont la même variable ; le seul test indépendant du verdict est `latence max < délai / 2`. Le verdict repose donc sur la lecture du code (attente par le netpoller) plus l'absence d'atteinte du délai : aucune réponse n'a attendu le délai. Les attentes de 75 à 131 ms (supérieures à ce que les autres sauts suggèrent) ne sont pas expliquées. Plan B non nécessaire.

### L4 : saut muet

Deux cas à distinguer : (a) « routeur muet puis routeur qui répond » (cas net) et (b) « muet puis cible » (les TTL muets entre le dernier routeur et la cible atteinte sont des sondes qui ont atteint la cible, pas des routeurs : exécutions 2 et 4, non comptées).

Première série (vers `1.1.1.1`) : cas net dans l'exécution 1 (TTL 7 muet, TTL 8 répond) et dans l'exécution à `PATH` vide (TTL 1 muet, TTL 2 répond), soit **1 exécution nette sur 5 plus `PATH` vide**. Exécutions 2 et 4 : cas (b) seulement. Exécutions 3 et 5 : aucun TTL ne répond après un muet.

Relance (5 exécutions, `-cycles 5 -extra-targets 8.8.8.8,9.9.9.9,208.67.222.222`, même procédure, binaire supprimé ensuite) : vers `1.1.1.1`, cas net dans les 5 exécutions (TTL 7 muet puis 8 répond ; TTL 1 muet puis 2 répond en plus dans 2 d'entre elles). Vers `8.8.8.8` : TTL 7 muet puis 8 répond dans 3 exécutions sur 5 (aucun muet dans les 2 autres). Vers `9.9.9.9` : cas net dans les 5 (TTL 7 muet puis 8 répond ; 10 muet puis 11 répond ; l'exécution 4 n'a que le TTL 10 muet puis 11 répond). `208.67.222.222` : non atteinte, non exploitée. Aucune exécution KO. Cumul : cas net observé dans 7 exécutions sur 11 vers `1.1.1.1` (exéc. 1, `PATH` vide, relance 1 à 5), plus les cibles `8.8.8.8` et `9.9.9.9`.

### L5 : arrêt en 30 s au plus, résultat explicite

| Cas | Résultat explicite | Durée (exéc. 1 à 5) |
|---|---|---|
| cible muette `192.0.2.1`, TTL max 30 | cible non atteinte, TTL maximum | 3.003 / 3.002 / 3.001 / 3.003 / 3.003 s |
| `1.1.1.1` avec TTL max abaissé à 5 | cible non atteinte, TTL maximum | 19 / 22 / 22 / 28 / 33 ms |
| `192.0.2.1`, délai global 1.5 s < durée de sonde 20 s | cible non atteinte, délai écoulé | 1.501 / 1.501 / 1.502 / 1.501 / 1.501 s |
| `1.1.1.1` atteinte | cible atteinte | voir tableau du trace principal |

Les trois résultats sont distincts dans les cinq exécutions, et tous les arrêts sont très inférieurs à 30 s. **Écart** : aucune cible dont le chemin dépasse réellement 30 sauts n'a été trouvée ; le cas « TTL maximum » est mesuré avec un TTL max abaissé à 5 et avec la cible muette.

### L6 : sondes en parallèle, moins de 5 s

| Exécution | Base de mesure | Durée |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | chemin réel (11 sauts >= 8) | 3.001 s |
| 2 | « chemin réel » (cible atteinte au TTL 23) | 3.001 s |
| 3 | cible non atteinte, TTL borné à 8 (consigné) | 3.001 s |
| 4 | « chemin réel » (cible atteinte au TTL 16) | 3.003 s |
| 5 | cible non atteinte, TTL borné à 8 (consigné) | 3.002 s |

Min / médiane / max : 3.001 / 3.001 / 3.003 s. Durée de sonde choisie : 3 s. Parallélisme : les exécutions 2 à 5 ont au moins 2 TTL muets (jusqu'à 24 TTL muets dans les exécutions 3 et 5) résolus ensemble en 3 s ; des délais en série dépasseraient largement 5 s. Un seul TTL muet (exécution 1) ne le prouve pas à lui seul. Limite : le test ne vérifie que la durée, pas la complétude du résultat (exécutions 3 et 5 : 6 sauts sur 8 répondent). La marge de 5 s dépend de la durée de sonde de 3 s.

### L7 : annulation sans fuite

100 cycles par exécution (annulation 150 ms après le début, vers la cible muette ; au moins 22 sondes non résolues à chaque annulation) : descripteurs 7 -> 7, goroutines 1 -> 1, dans les 5 exécutions. Les « maximums » (7 descripteurs, 1 goroutine) sont échantillonnés **après** chaque trace, pas pendant : ce n'est pas un pic (un trace ouvre environ 30 sockets). Les 2 goroutines vues dans l'exécution à `PATH` vide sont la goroutine d'annulation de la mesure, pas une fuite (1 après). Délai d'arrêt après annulation : min 108 à 119 µs, médiane 206 à 226 µs, max 367 à 723 µs. Aucune fuite, aucune correction nécessaire.

## Verdict par critère

| Critère | Verdict | Mesure clé | Effet de l'échec (feasibility.md) |
|---|---|---|---|
| L1 | OK | uid 1000, CapEff 0, `setsockopt` sans erreur, pas d'`os/exec`, `PATH` vide identique | Epic B abandonné |
| L2 | OK | 6 à 10 sauts avec adresse (5/5), minimum requis 3 | Epic B abandonné |
| L3 | OK (netpoller, lecture du code + délai jamais atteint) | attente max 131 ms pour un délai de 3 s | plan B, pas de no-go |
| L4 | OK (décision utilisateur : exécution sans cas net neutre) | cas net : exéc. 1 (TTL 7 → 8), `PATH` vide (TTL 1 → 2), 5/5 de la relance ; aucun KO | Epic B abandonné |
| L5 | OK (5/5) | arrêt en 3.0 s, trois résultats distincts | Epic B abandonné |
| L6 | OK (5/5, durée seulement) | 3.001 à 3.003 s ; N >= 8 sur 3 exéc., TTL borné à 8 sur 2 | seuil de S-03a assoupli, pas de no-go |
| L7 | OK (5/5) | 100 cycles, fd 7 -> 7, goroutines 1 -> 1 | correction puis re-mesure ; no-go si fuite structurelle |

## Verdict global

**Fonctionne** : aucun critère en échec, le trace natif sans privilège fonctionne sur Linux natif (Debian 13, noyau 6.12). Revue faite : aucun point bloquant.

## Décisions de l'utilisateur (interprétations)

- **L4** : une exécution sans « routeur muet puis routeur qui répond » est neutre ; L4 est OK si au moins une exécution observe le cas et qu'aucune n'est KO.
- **L6** : cible atteinte à un TTL N >= 8 => N est le chemin réel ; cible non atteinte => TTL borné à 8, consigné.
- **L5** : un TTL maximum abaissé à 5 plus la cible muette `192.0.2.1` suffisent pour le cas « TTL maximum ».

## Notes et limites de la mesure

- Variabilité : le nombre de sauts qui répondent varie d'une exécution à l'autre (hypothèse de limitation de débit ICMP avec 30 sondes simultanées, non vérifiée). À étudier pour S-03a (étaler les envois ?).
- L2 : « TTL croissants » est tautologique (les sauts sont rendus dans l'ordre des TTL) ; seul le minimum de 3 sauts avec adresse est réellement mesuré.
- L4 : « le trace ne s'arrête pas à un saut muet » est vrai par construction (sondes parallèles, un TTL ne dépend pas du précédent).
- L1 : le test à `PATH` vide n'est pas discriminant (le binaire n'exécute rien) ; l'import vérifié (pas d'`os/exec`) fait foi. « Aucun `sudo` » n'est pas mesuré : seuls uid et CapEff le sont.
- L5 : l'état « délai écoulé » exige une sonde de 20 s et un délai de 1,5 s ; le plafond de 30 s n'est jamais approché (arrêts à environ 3 s).
- L7 : ne couvre pas l'annulation pendant `Dial` ou `Write` (l'annulation à 150 ms tombe quand les sondes attendent en lecture).
- Course connue dans `spike/nettrace/main.go` (lignes 322 à 330, variable `cancelledAt` écrite par la goroutine d'annulation) : à corriger si le code est repris pour S-03a.

Délai d'arrêt après annulation : min 108 à 119 µs, médiane 206 à 226 µs, max 367 à 723 µs. Aucune fuite, aucune correction nécessaire.

## Verdict par critère

| Critère | Verdict | Mesure clé | Effet de l'échec (feasibility.md) |
|---|---|---|---|
| L1 | OK | uid 1000, CapEff 0, `setsockopt` sans erreur, pas d'`os/exec`, `PATH` vide identique | Epic B abandonné |
| L2 | OK | 6 à 10 sauts avec adresse (5/5), minimum requis 3 | Epic B abandonné |
| L3 | OK (netpoller, lecture du code + délai jamais atteint) | attente max 131 ms pour un délai de 3 s | plan B, pas de no-go |
| L4 | OK (décision utilisateur : exécution sans cas net neutre) | cas net : exéc. 1 (TTL 7 → 8), `PATH` vide (TTL 1 → 2), 5/5 de la relance ; aucun KO | Epic B abandonné |
| L5 | OK (5/5) | arrêt en 3.0 s, trois résultats distincts | Epic B abandonné |
| L6 | OK (5/5, durée seulement) | 3.001 à 3.003 s ; N >= 8 sur 3 exéc., TTL borné à 8 sur 2 | seuil de S-03a assoupli, pas de no-go |
| L7 | OK (5/5) | 100 cycles, fd 7 -> 7, goroutines 1 -> 1 | correction puis re-mesure ; no-go si fuite structurelle |

## Verdict global

**Fonctionne** : aucun critère en échec, le trace natif sans privilège fonctionne sur Linux natif (Debian 13, noyau 6.12). Revue faite : aucun point bloquant.

## Décisions de l'utilisateur (interprétations)

- **L4** : une exécution sans « routeur muet puis routeur qui répond » est neutre ; L4 est OK si au moins une exécution observe le cas et qu'aucune n'est KO.
- **L6** : cible atteinte à un TTL N >= 8 => N est le chemin réel ; cible non atteinte => TTL borné à 8, consigné.
- **L5** : un TTL maximum abaissé à 5 plus la cible muette `192.0.2.1` suffisent pour le cas « TTL maximum ».

## Notes et limites de la mesure

- Variabilité : le nombre de sauts qui répondent varie d'une exécution à l'autre (hypothèse de limitation de débit ICMP avec 30 sondes simultanées, non vérifiée). À étudier pour S-03a (étaler les envois ?).
- L2 : « TTL croissants » est tautologique (les sauts sont rendus dans l'ordre des TTL) ; seul le minimum de 3 sauts avec adresse est réellement mesuré.
- L4 : « le trace ne s'arrête pas à un saut muet » est vrai par construction (sondes parallèles, un TTL ne dépend pas du précédent).
- L1 : le test à `PATH` vide n'est pas discriminant (le binaire n'exécute rien) ; l'import vérifié (pas d'`os/exec`) fait foi. « Aucun `sudo` » n'est pas mesuré : seuls uid et CapEff le sont.
- L5 : l'état « délai écoulé » exige une sonde de 20 s et un délai de 1,5 s ; le plafond de 30 s n'est jamais approché (arrêts à environ 3 s).
- L7 : ne couvre pas l'annulation pendant `Dial` ou `Write` (l'annulation à 150 ms tombe quand les sondes attendent en lecture).
- Course connue dans `spike/nettrace/main.go` (lignes 322 à 330, variable `cancelledAt` écrite par la goroutine d'annulation) : à corriger si le code est repris pour S-03a.
